messages:
Maya Kline: FYI we got an escalation from customer CN-9102. They report streaming responses stopping mid-way; their client shows connection closed and user sees truncated output. Our console shows a 502 for the request so it landed as a platform 5xx. Ticket: https://zendesk.company/tickets/9102 :warning:

ops-bot: alert: streaming-5xx-rate-high (20/min over 10m) - channel: #support :bangbang:

Eli R.: need sample request + headers, region, model, and whether they're using hosted or dedicated. Also send gateway/nginx logs if possible.

Maya Kline: Hosted, region: eu-central-1, model: redwood-compat. Customer used the streaming chat endpoint via a mobile app. Their sample curl (auth stripped):

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-compat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"very long input..."}], "stream":true}'
```

Maya Kline: Gateway excerpt (sanitized):

```
[2026-11-14T09:41:02Z] gateway-eu-03: write() to client failed (Broken pipe), client: 18.204.33.72, request: "POST /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://runtime-45:8080/stream", host: "api.redwood.example"
[2026-11-14T09:41:02Z] 502 "POST /v1/chat/stream" 502 198 "-" "okhttp/4.9.3"
```

Maya Kline: Runtime shows last chunk delivered and then `recv() returned 0`, followed immediately by `connection reset by peer` in gateway. Customer insists no explicit cancel. Their app is Android on older devices over carrier network.

Samir Patel: This pattern looks like client-side TCP close while server still streaming. Our gateway currently treats that as a 502 and emits a 5xx metric. That's noisy for SRE and confuses support. We should differentiate "client aborted stream" from genuine backend error. Historically we've had similar noise but not at this volume.

Samir Patel: I ran a quick metric check: many of these 502s have Transfer-Encoding: chunked with final bytes sent <2s before socket error. Also tcp_rst counts rose for a handful of mobile IP ranges. Suggest we add a parse rule in gateway logs: if upstream response code 200 and error occurs during write with socket error -> classify as client_abort_stream (499-ish) and do not increment platform_5xx.

Eli R.: Can reproduce locally with a tiny server that streams SSE and then simulates abrupt client closure. Repro code below:

```python
# repro: streams then simulates client drop
import socketserver, http.server, time

class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','text/event-stream')
        self.send_header('Transfer-Encoding','chunked')
        self.end_headers()
        for i in range(10):
            data = f"data: {i}\n\n".encode()
            size = format(len(data), 'x').encode()
            self.wfile.write(size + b"\r\n" + data + b"\r\n")
            self.wfile.flush()
            time.sleep(0.3)
        # simulate client closing socket mid-stream
        try:
            self.request.shutdown(socketserver.SHUT_WR)
        except Exception:
            pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    http.server.HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0',8080),Handler).serve_forever()
```

Eli R.: hitting via gateway results in gateway log: "upstream prematurely closed while sending to client" and gateway returns 502.

Sophie Nguyen: Operational plan: 1) add an explicit metric counter for client_stream_aborts so we don't lose visibility; 2) change metrics pipeline to avoid counting these as 5xx in alerting; 3) short-term mute the streaming-5xx alert if most are client aborts. Also draft a support KB explaining mobile flaky networks and recommended client-side strategies.

Maya Kline: Customer asked for mitigations now. What do we recommend?

Sophie Nguyen: Short blurb you can send: "Partial streams are often due to intermittent network or OS-level TCP resets on mobile. Workarounds: implement client retry with resume or restart of the request, reduce the time between chunks so partial output is smaller, and send application-level keepalive pings. If possible, use wired/WiFi for long outputs. We're working on improving classification on our side so these won't be counted as 5xx."

Samir Patel: Action items and owners:
- Samir -> implement gateway log detection + emit metric `client_stream_abort_total` and tag with region/model (ETA: 48h, P1).
- Eli -> add repro under infra/streaming-repros and add automated test for gateway handling of client RST (ETA: 24h).
- Sophie -> write KB article + support snippet and provide to Maya (ETA: 12h).
- Maya -> share workaround with customer and confirm if temporary fix acceptable (ETA: today).

ops-bot: paging Samir Patel for P1 task: gateway-client-abort-detection - call: +1-555-0123

Samir Patel: I'll take it. Note: need to be careful to not misclassify real backend errors; rule should only fire when upstream response code is success and write fails with socket-level error immediately after chunk write. We'll also record both metrics (client_abort and backend_write_fail) for correlation.

Eli R.: PR queued for repro and unit test. Will cc @Sophie on alerting changes.

Maya Kline: customer tried retry/reconnect and saw improved results. They are fine waiting for internal changes. I'll close the Zendesk ticket after we have a patch in staging. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
